title: I Will Teach You To Be Rich

questions.q: What does Sethi say is the first step toward getting rich?
a: Accepting that you alone are responsible for your finances
Finding an employer with a generous retirement plan
Cutting every unnecessary expense from your budget
Waiting for the stock market to become less volatile
questions.why: The first lesson says excuses always stay excuses; taking responsibility is the start of getting rich.

questions.q: How does the book divide a paycheck under its Conscious Spending Plan?
a: 60% fixed costs, 10% investing, 10% savings, 20% fun
50% fixed costs, 20% investing, 20% savings, 10% fun
70% fixed costs, 10% investing, 10% savings, 10% fun
40% fixed costs, 20% investing, 30% savings, 10% fun
questions.why: The example automates 60% for fixed costs, 10% for investing, 10% for savings and leaves 20% guilt-free.

questions.q: Why does the summary recommend automating your savings and payments?
a: It removes the need to rely on willpower every month
It guarantees your investments will never lose value
It earns you a higher interest rate than manual saving
It lets you skip tracking where your money goes
questions.why: Automation works like any good habit: taking willpower out of the equation makes it easier to get right.

questions.q: What does the comparison of starting at 25 versus 35 show?
a: Starting a decade earlier outweighs investing a larger total
Investing a larger total always produces a bigger final fund
Older investors earn higher returns on the same amount
You should stop contributing once you turn 35
questions.why: The earlier starter invests $55,000 and ends with $615,000, while the later one invests $130,000 and ends with $431,000.

questions.q: What does the book suggest doing with a 401(k)?
a: Contribute enough to capture your employer's full match
Withdraw from it early to clear credit card debt
Use it to buy individual stocks you research yourself
Keep it in cash until you are close to retirement
questions.why: The summary advises maxing out your 401(k) so you get the most from your employer's matching contribution.
